messages:
sam: Heads-up: after last night's batching-v2 rollout we're seeing a sustained ~18% host CPU uplift on small streaming traffic (short prompts). Appears concentrated on ingress parsing + HPACK decode path.
chi: timeframe + regions? any spike windows?
sam: started 2026-03-22T06:12 UTC, noticed in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Correlates with bursty multiplexing from gateway. Quick top functions from a short pprof sample attached below.
perf-bot: deploy event: batching-v2 by @ci at 06:05 -> canary 15% -> promoted 06:06
sam: pprof top (sanitized):
```
# top 12
14.7% http2::hpack_decode
11.9% parse_proto_frame
10.6% kernel_selector::score_candidates
9.8% batch_coordinator::shrink_window
8.2% writev_flush
7.0% kv_cache::evict
6.4% tokenize::scan_utf8
5.1% grpc::enqueue_stream_chunk
4.0% telemetry::emit_metrics
3.0% sched::wakeup
2.3% http2::handle_frame
```
chi: kernel_selector::score_candidates being that high is suspicious. batching-v2 changed the coordinator to rescore per-inflight-chunk to avoid bad batching decisions. looks like scorer is now executed O(n) per chunk.
anika: if scorer runs per-chunk, combined with smaller windows (shrink_window) we lose batching and also churn kv cache because selector picks variant ids more often. that explains kv_cache::evict increase.
sam: yes KV eviction rate up ~9% and selector_call_count per-request jumped from ~1.2 to ~3.9 avg on short prompts.
devops: can we reproduce locally? chi any loadscript?
chi: i'll spin a small jittered load with short payloads to mimic multiplexing: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --latency 'lua_short_requests.lua' http://ingress:8080/v1/generate` where lua sends 40-60 token prompts with streaming. also gather `go tool pprof -http=:8081 /tmp/ingress.cpu` on the host.
anika: mitigation options: 1) fast-path scorer: if tokens<128 return last-decision for route (memoize) 2) increase batching window slightly (ms) to reduce chunk churn 3) make selector id stable (avoid ephemeral salt) so kv_cache keys remain stable 4) instrument selector call count + batch efficiency metric.
sam: agreed. immediate plan: roll back batching-v2 to restore prior behavior on canary, while we implement fast-path memoization and stable variant ids.
perf-bot: rollback requested at 06:22 by @sam -> rolling to canary 15% -> in progress
devops: note: changing batching window might slightly increase median latency for tiny requests. we'll tune to keep p95 SLA.
chi: follow-ups for engineering: - add selector memo keyed by (route, model_arch, quant_profile, short_len=true) - only call full scorer once per batch, not per chunk - add stable_variant_id hashing (use model-version + quant-profile, avoid timestamp) - emit metric `selector_calls_per_request` and `kv_evictions_per_minute`
anika: also add smallwrite/hpack telemetry: `hpack_decode_per_request` and `writev_flush_count`. helps see host pressure from http2 framing.
sam: i'm launching the rollback now; if rollback reduces CPU to baseline we'll proceed with bisection + patch. can someone run the wrk test and post pprof before/after?
chi: running now, will post links to traces + flamegraphs in this thread.
sam: thanks. i'll open an issue with action items and assign eng-runtime perf. tagging @eng-runtime. :eyes:
